Coefficients of the near-surface temperature difference

Source: R/metric-dt.R
ef_dt_coef.Rd

Solves the coefficients of the linear relation \(dT = a + b\,T_{s,datum}\) of METRIC from the near-surface temperature differences required at the hot and cold anchor pixels. The relation reproduces both anchor values exactly.

Usage

ef_dt_coef(ts_datum_hot, ts_datum_cold, dt_hot, dt_cold)

Arguments

ts_datum_hot, ts_datum_cold

Numeric. Datum temperature of the hot and cold anchor [K] (see ef_ts_datum()). Must be finite and > 0, with ts_datum_hot > ts_datum_cold.

dt_hot, dt_cold

Numeric. Near-surface temperature difference required at the hot and cold anchor [K]. Must be finite.

Value

A list with elements a (intercept [K]) and b (slope [-]), numeric vectors with the common length of the inputs (one pair per calibration, e.g. per scene) keeping their dim.

Details

$$b = \frac{dT_{hot} - dT_{cold}}{T_{s,datum,hot} - T_{s,datum,cold}}, \qquad a = dT_{cold} - b\,T_{s,datum,cold}$$

Notation: a is the intercept and b the slope, as in dev/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md; the water package uses the opposite names.

Pixels outside the range of the anchors use the same line (extrapolation, flagged by ef_calibrate_h()). A slope b <= 0 with well-ordered anchors contradicts the METRIC assumption that \(dT\) grows with the surface temperature: it is returned unchanged here and flagged (EF_H_DT_SLOPE_NONPOSITIVE, critical) by ef_calibrate_h().

Missing values propagate. ts_datum_hot <= ts_datum_cold (equal datum temperatures leave b undefined; a lower hot temperature suggests swapped anchors) raises an error of class earthflux_calibration_error. Other values outside the domain raise earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error).

Verification status: CANDIDATA (form observed in the water package and in dev/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md section 3; Allen et al., 2007, not consulted, including a reported erratum in its intercept equation).

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

See also

Other aerodynamics and sensible heat functions: ef_air_density(), ef_blending_wind(), ef_calibrate_h(), ef_h_control(), ef_rah(), ef_sensible_heat(), ef_ts_datum(), ef_ustar(), ef_zom()

Examples

ef_dt_coef(ts_datum_hot = 317.298, ts_datum_cold = 300,
           dt_hot = 11.733091, dt_cold = 0.675211)
#> $a
#> [1] -191.1021
#> 
#> $b
#> [1] 0.6392577
#>
